items.title: Hytale Server on Docker
items.text: Run a Hytale dedicated server with automatic downloads, persistent login, mod management and tools for diagnosing problems. Start with one Docker Compose service; add Kubernetes, a token broker or a referral router when you need them.

items.title: Before you start
items.text:
• The image supports AMD64 and ARM64. Java runs natively on both. On ARM64, only the official downloader uses the bundled emulator.
  • Hytale uses UDP. Publish 5520/udp and allow the chosen port through your firewall.
  • Persist the complete /data volume to keep worlds, mods, configuration and login state.
  • First startup has two separate authorizations: one to download the files and one to authenticate the running server. Both prompts appear in the logs.

items.title: Images and documentation versions
items.text:
Use hybrowse/hytale-server from Docker Hub or its GHCR mirror. Pin a published image tag for deployments you want to reproduce.

These docs follow the repository's main branch. For changes in a specific image version, see the release notes.

items.title: Get help
items.text:
Use troubleshooting first. For support, include your image version, deployment method and an allowlisted diagnostic report when available. Review anything you share publicly and keep login credentials private.

Ask in Discord or open a GitHub issue. For Hytale's own server behavior, refer to the official server manual.

This is an unofficial community project. The image does not contain proprietary game files. See the repository's license and policy notes.

items.title: Maintain and preview the docs
items.text: Documentation lives in docs/ and is built with Zensical. Edit Markdown in the same PR as the feature it describes. Keep instructions in English, use plain punctuation and explain what a user should see after running a command.

items.title: Local preview
items.text:
From a checkout of this repository, create an isolated Python environment:

python3 -m venv .venv-docs
.venv-docs/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements-docs.txt
.venv-docs/bin/zensical serve

Open the local address printed by the preview server. The local URL is different from the public GitHub Pages project path; always run the built-site checks too.

On Windows, use .venv-docs\Scripts\python and .venv-docs\Scripts\zensical instead.

items.title: Build and check
items.text:
.venv-docs/bin/zensical build --clean --strict
.venv-docs/bin/python ci/check-docs.py
.venv-docs/bin/python -m unittest discover -s ci -p 'test_pages.py'

The checks cover navigation, rendered links and anchors, documented environment variables and shared publication of docs and Helm artifacts. PR builds upload the generated site as a workflow artifact; they do not publish it.

Examples should use hytale as the Compose service name, clearly mark partial snippets, quote environment values and avoid real credentials. Keep deployment examples consistent with the scripts and manifests. Do not promise a live server is authenticated based only on a process, socket or probe.

items.title: Publication
items.text:
The Documentation and Helm workflow is the only writer of the gh-pages branch. It runs after changes to docs and relevant configuration on main, on a published release, or manually. GitHub Pages keeps its existing branch-based source (gh-pages, root).

A docs update carries forward the existing root index.yaml, every published hytale-server-*.tgz and any CNAME, then replaces generated documentation. A release adds its chart from the release tag and merges its entry into the Helm index. Docs are built from current main, including on release runs, so publishing an older game-image release does not revert the website.

Publication jobs share a queue that does not cancel pending release jobs. Build, link and preservation checks must pass before the branch changes. Historical charts keep their names and the existing Helm repository URL remains:

https://hybrowse.github.io/hytale-server-docker

The workflow explicitly requests a GitHub Pages build after updating the branch. This avoids relying on a push made with GITHUB_TOKEN to trigger another workflow. A manual workflow run can retry publication without creating a release. It never publishes a new chart unless triggered by a release.

items.title: Compatibility and releases
items.text:
These docs track main. Mark features that are not yet available in published images. Link to release notes for compatibility details. Keep navigation, examples and links consistent when reorganizing pages.

Refer to the official manual for upstream requirements and policies. Every documentation page must have a place in the navigation; do not keep parallel copies or placeholder pages.

items.title: Authentication
items.text:
The downloader login, server login and optional broker have different jobs.

Login Purpose Stored state Downloader Obtain server files and assets /data/.hytale-downloader-credentials.json Server Authenticate the running server for player connections /data/server/auth.enc, configuration, identity/key Broker (optional) Supply short-lived server tokens for automated deployments Long-lived state stays with the broker

Completing the downloader login does not authenticate the running server.

items.title: Sign in to the server
items.text:
In HYTALE_AUTH_MODE=authenticated mode, the server must be authenticated after startup before players can connect. This is separate from the downloader OAuth flow used for auto-download.

On a fresh server, HYTALE_AUTO_AUTH=true (default) queues Hytale's own /auth persistence Encrypted and /auth login device commands. Follow the device login link in the logs. If several profiles are offered, run hytale-cli auth select <name-or-number> and check the result in the server logs.

Stored credentials and broker/supplied tokens bypass this first-start action. Set HYTALE_AUTO_AUTH=false for manual login. Automatic login requires HYTALE_CONSOLE_PIPE=true; validation, schema export, help and offline runs skip it. hytale-cli auth login starts another persistent device login when needed.

See:

  • quickstart.md

Advanced (providers / fleets):

  • Broker integration (tokens via HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN / HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN)

items.title: Preserve authentication across restarts
items.text: Keep the complete /data volume, including .machine-id, server/auth.enc, server/config.json and any server/auth.key. If you supply HYTALE_AUTH_KEY_FILE, keep that Secret too. Do not reset server credentials to fix an expired downloader login.

items.title: Providers and fleets
items.text: See broker integration. Broker sessions do not authorize native game-update downloads.

items.title: If login fails
items.text: Use Doctor for local checks and troubleshooting for specific symptoms. hytale-cli auth status writes the live status to the server logs; it is separate from the read-only hytale-cli status alias.

items.title: Overview
items.text:
The Hytale dedicated server supports an internal backup mechanism. This image exposes it via environment variables and recommends storing backups on a separate volume.

Until we have more operational experience with the official server, treat backup outputs as opaque artifacts.

items.title: Enable backups (Docker Compose)
items.text:
services:
  hytale:
    image: hybrowse/hytale-server:latest
    ports:
      - "5520:5520/udp"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
      - ./backups:/backups
    environment:
      HYTALE_ENABLE_BACKUP: "true"
      HYTALE_BACKUP_DIR: "/backups"
      HYTALE_BACKUP_FREQUENCY_MINUTES: "60"
    restart: unless-stopped

items.title: Recommended storage patterns
items.text:
• Keep /data (server state) and backups on different volumes/paths.
  • Consider syncing ./backups to offsite storage (object storage, rsync to another host, etc.).

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• If you change backup paths, ensure the container user can write to them.
  • Backup settings map directly to the server flags (--backup, --backup-dir, --backup-frequency).
  • If HYTALE_ENABLE_BACKUP=true and HYTALE_BACKUP_DIR is not set, this image defaults the backup directory to /data/backups.

items.title: Console commands and diagnostics
items.text:
Run hytale-cli inside the server container with docker compose exec hytale. Kubernetes users can use kubectl exec <pod> -c hytale-server -- instead.

Command What it does hytale-cli auth login Queue encrypted persistence and a server device login hytale-cli auth select <name-or-number> Select a profile offered by Hytale hytale-cli auth status Send an auth-status request; read the result in server logs hytale-cli send <command> Send a command to the live console hytale-cli doctor Read-only local diagnostic checks hytale-cli status Same checks as doctor, not live auth status hytale-cli report Allowlisted JSON diagnostic report

items.title: Send a command
items.text:
docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli send "/say Server restart in five minutes"

Console commands require a running server and the default HYTALE_CONSOLE_PIPE=true. They queue commands rather than returning the server's response; read the logs afterward.

Send multiple commands from standard input:

printf '%s\n' '/auth status' '/say Maintenance complete' | docker compose exec -T hytale hytale-cli send

Setting HYTALE_CONSOLE_PIPE=false disables console injection and automatic first-start login. Read-only diagnostics still work. The FIFO path can be changed with HYTALE_CONSOLE_FIFO; normally the default /tmp/hytale-console.fifo is sufficient.

items.title: Collect a support report
items.text:
docker compose exec -T hytale hytale-cli report > hytale-report.json

The redirection writes the file on your host. See Doctor for privacy, flags, exit codes and the distinction between local checks and live server readiness.

items.title: Configure server and mod JSON files
items.text: Use HYTALE_CONFIG_* for common server settings. Use CFG_* when a JSON file already contains placeholders. Both run before Java starts.

items.title: Server config patching (HYTALE_CONFIG_*)
items.text:
On startup, this image ensures /data/server/config.json exists:

  • If missing, it is created from a bundled default template.
  • Then optional HYTALE_CONFIG_* overrides are applied.
  • If the template is unavailable, the image does not pre-create config.json; the server creates it on first start. In that case, HYTALE_CONFIG_* overrides are skipped for that startup.

This works for both first start and existing servers and does not require ${CFG_*} placeholders.

Convenience overrides:

  • HYTALE_CONFIG_SERVER_NAME
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_MOTD
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_PASSWORD (secret)
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_MAX_PLAYERS
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_MAX_VIEW_RADIUS
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_DEFAULT_WORLD
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_DEFAULT_GAME_MODE

Advanced overrides:

  • HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON (must be a JSON object)
  • HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON_SRC (path to a file containing a JSON object)

HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON and HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON_SRC are mutually exclusive.

Patch behavior:

  • Existing keys not mentioned in overrides are preserved.
  • Nested objects are merged recursively.
  • Convenience variables override conflicting keys from HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON.
  • Invalid JSON or invalid numeric values fail startup early (no partial writes).

Example:

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      HYTALE_CONFIG_SERVER_NAME: "My Server"
      HYTALE_CONFIG_MOTD: "Welcome"
      HYTALE_CONFIG_MAX_PLAYERS: "50"
      HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON: '{"Defaults":{"World":"creative-island"}}'

items.title: Config file interpolation (CFG_*)
items.text:
On startup, this image can replace placeholders in JSON config files using environment variables.

By default, only /data/server/config.json is processed. With HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_MODE=all, JSON files under /data/server/mods/ and HYTALE_MODS_PATH are processed too. Use explicit mode to choose additional paths.

Interpolation runs after CurseForge mod installation (if enabled) and before the server process is started.

items.title: Placeholders
items.text:
The entrypoint searches JSON string values for references to variables prefixed with CFG_. You can use:

  • ${CFG_FOO}
  • $CFG_FOO

items.title: Typing rules (important)
items.text:
There are two modes:

  • If a JSON string value is exactly a placeholder, for example:

    • "${CFG_MAX_PLAYERS}"

then the value is replaced with a typed JSON value when possible. The environment variable is interpreted as JSON via jq fromjson. Examples:

- `CFG_MAX_PLAYERS=20` becomes `20`
- `CFG_PUBLIC=true` becomes `true`
- `CFG_NAME='"My Server"'` becomes `"My Server"`
- `CFG_OBJ='{"a":1}'` becomes `{ "a": 1 }`

If parsing as JSON fails, the value is used as a normal string.

  • If the placeholder appears inside a larger string, for example:

    • "Welcome to ${CFG_SERVER_NAME}!"

then the variable value is substituted as plain text.

items.title: Enable/disable
items.text:
• Enabled by default.

  • To disable interpolation entirely, set:

    • HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION=false

items.title: Scope / performance / safety controls
items.text:
To reduce startup time and avoid applying interpolation to plugin-generated data files, you can scope interpolation.

Modes:

  • HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_MODE=server-only (default)

    • Only interpolates /data/server/config.json

  • HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_MODE=all

    • Always interpolates /data/server/config.json
    • Also interpolates JSON files under /data/server/mods/ and HYTALE_MODS_PATH

  • HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_MODE=explicit

    • Always interpolates /data/server/config.json
    • Additionally interpolates only the paths listed in HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_PATHS

HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_PATHS accepts space-separated paths. Each entry can be:

  • a file (relative to /data/server/ or an absolute path)
  • a directory (all *.json files beneath it will be processed)

Optional limits:

  • HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_MAX_BYTES (empty by default)

    • If set to a number, skips JSON files larger than this size.

  • HYTALE_CFG_INTERPOLATION_EXCLUDE_PATHS (empty by default)

    • Space-separated shell glob patterns matched against the full file path.
    • If a file matches, it is skipped.

Security note:

  • CFG_* can be used for secrets if plugins only support secrets via config files.
  • To reduce risk of accidental substitution into large/untrusted plugin-generated files (or files that might be exposed to players), prefer server-only or explicit.

items.title: Example
items.text:
services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      CFG_SERVER_NAME: "My Server"
      CFG_MAX_PLAYERS: "20"

In JSON:

{
  "name": "${CFG_SERVER_NAME}",
  "maxPlayers": "${CFG_MAX_PLAYERS}"
}

items.title: CurseForge Mods
items.text:
This image supports automatic mod download and updates from CurseForge.

You can configure mods via environment variables, and the container will install (and optionally update) mods on startup.

items.title: Why this is useful
items.text:
• Fully automated mod provisioning (no manual downloads)
  • Automatic updates on container restart (optional)
  • Managed mods are stored separately from any manually installed mods
  • Idempotent installs via a local manifest on the /data volume

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• A CurseForge API key (required)
  • Internet access to https://api.curseforge.com and the CurseForge CDN

items.title: Getting an API key
items.text:
1. Go to console.curseforge.com
  2. Create an API key
  3. Copy your API key

Important: CurseForge API keys start with $2a$10$. If your key doesn't look like this, it may be incorrectly formatted.

items.title: Docker Compose escaping
items.text:
In Docker Compose YAML, dollar signs ($) must be escaped as $$. If you set the key directly in the YAML (not recommended), you need:

HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY: "$$2a$$10$$YourKeyHere..."

Recommended: Use a secret file instead to avoid escaping issues:

HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY_SRC: "/run/secrets/curseforge_api_key"
secrets:
  curseforge_api_key:
    file: ./secrets/curseforge_api_key.txt

The file should contain the API key as-is (with normal $ signs, no escaping).

items.title: Quickstart (Docker Compose)
items.text:
services:
  hytale:
    image: hybrowse/hytale-server:latest
    environment:
      HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD: "true"

      # Enable CurseForge mod management
      HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS: |
        123456
        234567:3456789

      # Read the API key from a mounted secret file
      HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY_SRC: "/run/secrets/curseforge_api_key"

    secrets:
      - curseforge_api_key

    ports:
      - "5520:5520/udp"
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data
    tty: true
    stdin_open: true
    restart: unless-stopped

secrets:
  curseforge_api_key:
    file: ./secrets/curseforge_api_key.txt

Notes:

  • If HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS is set and you did not explicitly set HYTALE_MODS_PATH, the image defaults it to /data/server/mods-curseforge.
  • The default mods/ folder of the Hytale server remains unaffected.

items.title: Mod reference formats
items.text:
HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS supports a whitespace / newline separated list.

  • 123456
    • Install the latest file for CurseForge project with ID 123456 (can be found in the sidebar of the mod's page)
  • 123456:3456789
    • Install a specific file with ID 3456789 for CurseForge project with ID 123456
  • 123456@server
    • Pick the latest file whose fileName or displayName contains server for CurseForge project with ID 123456
  • @/path/to/mods.txt
    • Load additional entries from a file inside the container

items.title: Environment variables
items.text: Variable Default Description HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS (empty) Enables CurseForge mod management and lists mod references. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY (empty) CurseForge API key (secret). Prefer *_SRC in production. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY_SRC (empty) Path to a file containing the API key (Docker secrets recommended). HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_AUTO_UPDATE true If true, checks for updates on startup (downloads only when needed). If false, keeps an already installed version. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_RELEASE_CHANNEL release Allowed channels: release, beta, alpha, any. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_GAME_VERSION_FILTER (empty) Filters gameVersions[] in the CurseForge API response. Leave empty to accept all versions. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_CHECK_INTERVAL_SECONDS 0 If > 0, skips remote checks when the last check was recent (reduces API usage on frequent restarts). HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_PRUNE true when mods path is not /data/server/mods, otherwise false If true, removes previously installed CurseForge mods that are no longer listed in HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_FAIL_ON_ERROR false If true, fails container startup when any configured mod cannot be resolved/installed. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_LOCK true If false, disables the CurseForge install lock (power users). HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_HTTP_CACHE_URL (empty) Optional HTTP cache gateway base URL used for both API requests and file downloads. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_HTTP_CACHE_API_URL (empty) Optional HTTP cache gateway base URL used for CurseForge API requests only. Defaults to HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_HTTP_CACHE_URL. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_HTTP_CACHE_DOWNLOAD_URL (empty) Optional HTTP cache gateway base URL used for mod file downloads only. Defaults to HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_HTTP_CACHE_URL. HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_DEBUG false If true, prints additional diagnostics on API and download failures (does not print the API key).

items.title: Optional: HTTP cache gateway (for ephemeral servers)
items.text:
If you start many short-lived servers without a persistent /data volume, you may want to reduce CurseForge API usage and avoid repeatedly downloading the same mod files.

You can point the container at an internal HTTP cache gateway (for example Varnish + Caddy):

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_HTTP_CACHE_URL: "http://curseforge-cache:8080"

When these variables are set, the image routes both CurseForge API calls and file downloads through the cache gateway while preserving the original Host header. This allows the gateway to forward requests to the correct upstream (api.curseforge.com, edge.forgecdn.net, ...).

items.title: Mods directory
items.text:
• Visible mods directory (passed as --mods):
    • /data/server/mods-curseforge (default when CurseForge is enabled)
    • Or whatever you set HYTALE_MODS_PATH to

The image installs each mod file and then creates a stable file in the visible directory:

  • cf-<modId>-<fileId>-<fileName>

This avoids filename collisions and makes updates deterministic.

items.title: State directory (manifest, downloads)
items.text:
State is stored on the /data volume under:

  • /data/.hytale-curseforge-mods/

Files:

  • manifest.json stores the installed file IDs and last check timestamp

items.title: Lock
items.text:
To prevent concurrent installations into the same /data volume, the image uses a lock:

  • /data/.hytale-curseforge-mods-lock

items.title: Production strategies: dependency conflicts and version mismatches
items.text:
CurseForge projects can have optional or required dependencies, and multiple mods may ship incompatible versions of shared libraries. The image does not attempt to solve a dependency graph or resolve conflicts automatically. In production, treat the mod list as a versioned input and use repeatable rollouts.

  • Pin exact file IDs for stability

    • Prefer modId:fileId for all critical mods.
    • This avoids unexpected updates when containers restart.

  • Freeze updates during normal operation

    • Set HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_AUTO_UPDATE=false to prevent silent drift.
    • If you want periodic updates, use a staging environment and promote the pinned file IDs into production.

  • Staged rollouts (canary) instead of updating everything at once

    • Maintain the mod list in a single source of truth (for example a file you mount and reference via @/path/to/mods.txt).
    • Roll out changes to a single instance first, validate startup and gameplay, then expand to the full fleet.

  • Make dependencies explicit

    • If a mod requires another CurseForge project, list the dependency explicitly in HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS.
    • If you rely on keyword selection (modId@keyword), prefer migrating to modId:fileId once you have identified a known-good version.

  • Avoid cross-instance mismatches

    • Ensure all instances use the same mod list and the same update policy.
    • If instances share a persistent /data volume, keep HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_LOCK=true to avoid concurrent installs.
    • If instances do not share /data, pinning file IDs is the most reliable way to keep versions aligned.

  • Operational troubleshooting (conflicts / crashes)

    • If startup crashes after a mod update, temporarily pin the previously working file ID and restart.
    • Use HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_FAIL_ON_ERROR=true to prevent starting with a partially installed mod set.
    • If you suspect a specific mod conflict, bisect by removing half the mods, then narrow down until the problematic entry is found.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
• If the container logs warn about a missing API key:

    • set HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY or HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY_SRC
    • set HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_FAIL_ON_ERROR=true if you want missing/failed mods to block startup

  • If a mod cannot be resolved:

    • verify the numeric project ID / file ID
    • try pinning a specific file via modId:fileId
    • if using HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_GAME_VERSION_FILTER, verify it matches the mod's file metadata

items.title: Data and permissions
items.text:
Keep the entire /data volume between container replacements. Reusing only the world directory loses other state needed for a predictable restart.

Path Purpose /data/Assets.zip Official assets, matched to the server release /data/server/HytaleServer.jar Official server binary /data/server/universe/ Default world and player data /data/server/config.json Server settings and saved profile configuration /data/server/mods/ Default mod directory /data/server/mods-curseforge/ Default additional directory for managed CurseForge mods /data/server/auth.enc Encrypted server login /data/server/auth.key Auth key when Hytale creates or uses one; treat as a secret /data/.machine-id Persistent machine identity /data/.hytale-downloader-credentials.json Separate downloader login; treat as a secret /data/updater/ Native-update staging, transactions and previous binaries /data/backups/ Default backup destination when built-in backups are enabled

Custom path settings can change some locations. See the variable reference.

items.title: Named volume or bind mount
items.text:
The quickstart uses a named volume. Docker manages its host location and initial ownership. A bind mount makes files visible in a host directory:

services:
  hytale:
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

This is a replacement for the quickstart's volume mount, not an additional mount at the same path. The image runs as UID/GID 1000:1000 by default. On Linux, create the host directory with ownership that lets that user write:

mkdir -p ./data
sudo chown 1000:1000 ./data

For an existing directory, inspect ownership before making recursive changes. Do not solve a permission error by deleting the data directory or running the game server as root.

items.title: Capacity and temporary files
items.text:
Allow room for assets, worlds, mods, backups and update copies. Native updates can temporarily need several copies of the game files. The Kubernetes examples use 20Gi for a basic claim and 40Gi for native updates; neither is a workload guarantee.

Keep /tmp writable. Large extraction jobs can consume substantial temporary storage; a RAM-backed temporary filesystem counts against container memory. Kubernetes defaults use disk-backed temporary storage.

items.title: One writer per world
items.text:
Never start two game-server processes against the same world volume. A second process can damage state even if the storage permits multiple mounts. For manual maintenance, stop the old process and wait for it to exit before using a replacement container or recovery Job.

See Kubernetes operations for PVC and rollout considerations and security for Secret handling.

items.text: This repository is intentionally set up so contributors can test the image locally without committing or redistributing proprietary Hytale server binaries.

To avoid manual provisioning steps, you can start the container with auto-download enabled:

Notes:

items.title: Apple Silicon (ARM64)
items.text:
Use the native ARM64 image for auto-download. The image includes emulation for only the official downloader; Java and the game server remain native. No --platform linux/amd64 override is required.

task dev:up:auto:amd64 is still available when you explicitly want to test the AMD64 image through emulation; it is not needed for normal ARM64 development.
