items.text:
The Hytale server provides an interactive console while the process is running.

Attach to the console:

task dev:attach

Detach without stopping the server:

  • Press Ctrl-p then Ctrl-q

items.title: Useful variables
items.text:
You can override these Task vars:

  • IMAGE_NAME (default hytale-server:local)
  • DEV_CONTAINER_NAME (default hytale-server-dev)
  • DEV_DATA_DIR (default ./data)
  • DEV_PORT (default 5520)

Example:

DEV_PORT=5521 task dev:up

items.title: Diagnostic checks
items.text:
The read-only diagnostic executable is built from diagnostics/ with Go's standard library. Go is only present in the build stage; the final image receives a static executable. The build runs its unit tests on the build platform and cross-compiles for the target architecture.

cd diagnostics
go test -race ./...
go vet ./...
# From the repository root, after building the image:
IMAGE_NAME=hytale-server:test sh ci/test-diagnostics.sh

Keep report fields allowlisted: do not add raw errors, arbitrary configuration, process arguments, filenames, account identifiers or log excerpts. Tests use synthetic secrets and fail if these appear in the serialized report. New checks must distinguish absence, an observed failure, and facts that cannot be established without contacting or changing a running server. Keep network checks opt-in and never use them to refresh credentials or mint a game session.

items.title: Doctor and support reports
items.text:
Run diagnostics inside the server container:

docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli doctor
# Same checks, JSON output suitable for a support request:
docker compose exec -T hytale hytale-cli report > hytale-report.json

Replace hytale with your Compose service name. With Kubernetes, use kubectl exec <pod> -- hytale-cli doctor (select the server container with -c if necessary). hytale-cli status is an alias for doctor.

Diagnostics also work with console injection disabled. They never start Java, run mods or the downloader, send console commands, change files, initiate login, refresh tokens, or mint game sessions. By default, they make no network requests. The existing container health check is unchanged.

items.title: What is checked
items.text:
• Image version (release builds), architecture, Java release metadata and ARM64 downloader emulator.
  • Server JAR and assets ZIP structure, readable configuration and selected invalid or conflicting settings.
  • Data, server, temporary and backup directory permissions; free space, inodes and estimated update space.
  • Cgroup memory and CPU quotas, explicit heap limits and estimated native-memory headroom.
  • Matching Java processes and the configured UDP port in the container's network namespace.
  • Presence and permissions of persistent authentication and downloader credentials, explicit token expiry when readable, and broker configuration.
  • Persistent authentication identity, update configuration, staging/transaction/lock remnants and required AOT files.
  • Mod archive counts and ZIP structure, without running mod code or reporting mod names.

An archive directory check does not read every asset. For a full ZIP CRC check:

docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli doctor --verify-archives

This streams all archive entries without extracting them and can take several minutes and substantial disk I/O. Neither mode proves that JAR and assets belong to the same release, or that mods are compatible with the server.

Space and heap headroom recommendations are estimates. Capacity needs depend on world size, players, mods and backup retention. A detected update lock or staging directory can belong to an active update; check the server before removing it.

items.title: Optional network checks
items.text:
docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli doctor --network --timeout 15s

This sends credential-free HTTPS HEAD requests to the Hytale OAuth endpoint and downloader archive, plus a GET to the configured broker's /healthz when enabled. It follows no redirects, sends no bearer token, and does not download server files. Broker URLs containing user information, a query or a fragment are skipped. The total network budget defaults to 10 seconds (maximum 30), starting after local checks. It does not bound local archive verification.

HTTP responses only establish transport reachability; broker health does not establish that an account can mint sessions. Proxy settings from the environment may be used by the HTTP client. Endpoint URLs and response bodies are not reported.

items.title: Interpreting results
items.text:
Each check has a stable ID, a status and, where useful, a suggested next step:

Status Meaning ok The specific local check passed. info An observation, not a readiness guarantee. warning A possible problem or a prerequisite that needs attention. error A detected local problem. unknown Cannot be established with this read-only inspection.

The report summary is error, warning or ok, in that order of precedence. ok means no local warning or error was found; unknown checks remain unknown. Exit codes are 0 without errors, 1 with errors, or 2 for invalid options. --strict also returns 1 for warnings. Unknown checks do not fail the command.

In particular:

  • An auth.enc file does not prove that it can be decrypted or that a live server is authenticated.
  • Token expiry checks do not validate signatures. An expired downloader access token does not imply that its refresh token is unusable.
  • A UDP socket does not prove that it belongs to Hytale, that Docker published the port, or that a firewall/router allows players through.
  • Java metadata describes the configured runtime, not necessarily a custom running JVM.

Use server logs and hytale-cli auth status for live authentication evidence. Use a real Hytale client from another network to verify external connectivity.

items.title: Sharing a report
items.text:
report and doctor --json use the same allowlisted JSON schema (schema_version: 1). They include fixed diagnostic messages, numeric observations and validated numeric version strings. They do not copy logs, environment dumps, configuration values, passwords, tokens, profile/account names, arbitrary paths, URLs, process arguments or raw exception messages. Human-readable output follows the same rules.

The report still describes your deployment (for example memory limits and enabled features). Review it before posting publicly. Keep logs and credentials separate. New checks may be added; consumers should tolerate unknown check IDs and fields.

If the container cannot start, inspect the mounted data without its entrypoint:

docker compose run --rm --no-deps --entrypoint hytale-cli hytale doctor --json

This diagnoses a separate container. A missing Java process or UDP listener is expected in that case, and it cannot inspect the stopped container's runtime. The diagnostic itself does not write to the mounted data.

items.title: Downloads and credentials
items.text:
If HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true and Assets.zip / HytaleServer.jar are missing, the container will:

  • download the official Hytale Downloader from https://downloader.hytale.com/
  • run it using the OAuth device-code flow
  • store downloader credentials on the /data volume
  • extract Assets.zip to /data/Assets.zip
  • extract Server/ contents to /data/server/

When HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, the container will check for updates on each start by comparing the remote version against the locally stored version (in .hytale-version). Downloads only happen when an update is available. Set HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=false to disable update checks entirely and only download when files are missing.

Credentials are stored as:

  • /data/.hytale-downloader-credentials.json

If that file already exists (for example from a previous run), downloads become non-interactive.

To replace an expired or revoked login, set HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_RESET_CREDENTIALS=true for one startup and complete the device login shown in the logs. Remove the setting once signed in: leaving it enabled clears the downloader login on every startup. This only resets downloader credentials; server authentication, worlds and configuration are preserved. It cannot be combined with HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC; replace the mounted credentials instead. See recovery steps.

For non-interactive operations (providers/fleets), use one of these patterns:

  • Seed downloader credentials via HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC (recommended if you keep HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true).
  • Provision Assets.zip and Server/ out-of-band (for example with an init container) and run with HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=false.

If you want fully non-interactive automation, see: Non-interactive auto-download (seed credentials)

For safety, HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_URL is restricted to https://downloader.hytale.com/.

Auto-download works on both linux/amd64 and linux/arm64. The official archive currently provides an x86-64 downloader only. On ARM64, the image runs that helper through QEMU user-mode emulation, including its version checks. Java and the Hytale server remain native ARM64. No privileged mode or host binfmt registration is required. AMD64 images do not install the emulator. Manual provisioning remains available; see server-files.md.

items.title: Seed an existing downloader login
items.text:
If you already have .hytale-downloader-credentials.json, you can mount it read-only and seed it:

services:
  hytale:
    secrets:
      - hytale_downloader_credentials
    environment:
      HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD: "true"
      HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC: "/run/secrets/hytale_downloader_credentials"

secrets:
  hytale_downloader_credentials:
    file: ./secrets/.hytale-downloader-credentials.json

items.title: Kubernetes operations
items.text: Use this page after installing the chart or choosing a Kustomize overlay. Keep your namespace and release name consistent across commands.

items.title: Important: server files and persistence
items.text:
The container expects its data under /data:

  • /data/Assets.zip
  • /data/server/HytaleServer.jar

Whether you persist /data depends on your operation model:

  • If you want the server files, mods, backups, and generated state to survive restarts, use a PVC.
  • If you want fully ephemeral nodes and sync state elsewhere (e.g. an external backup/sync process), you can run without a PVC.

If you enable auto-download (HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true), the server files can be downloaded at runtime into /data.

Note: We intentionally do not enable a read-only root filesystem by default. The official server workflow can require writing a machine-id (and while the image has workarounds, a strictly read-only root filesystem can still be surprising operationally).

items.title: Recommended production patterns for server files
items.text:
For non-interactive Kubernetes operations, prefer one of these:

  • Keep HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true and mount a downloader credentials secret as HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC.
  • Set HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=false and provision /data/Assets.zip + /data/server/ before container startup (for example with an init container).

Why this matters: Session Token Broker runs later in startup. If auto-download is still waiting for first-time auth (or fails), broker logs/calls are not reached yet.

items.title: First startup and profile selection
items.text:
For the following examples, run commands in the server namespace (kubectl -n <namespace>). The examples live in the source repository; download them or run Helm from a checkout. For example, install the published image with the first-start values file:

helm upgrade --install hytale ./deploy/helm/hytale-server \
  -f deploy/helm/hytale-server/examples/first-start.yaml
kubectl get pods -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=hytale
kubectl logs -f <pod> -c hytale-server

There are two independent logins: the downloader login before Java starts, then Hytale's server login, which the image starts automatically on a fresh installation. Both URLs/codes appear in the logs. If Hytale lists several profiles:

kubectl exec <pod> -c hytale-server -- hytale-cli auth select <name-or-number>
kubectl exec <pod> -c hytale-server -- hytale-cli auth status

No terminal attachment or stdin/tty setting is needed. Use hytale-cli auth login to start a login manually. HYTALE_AUTO_AUTH=false opts out. Stored credentials, broker authentication and supplied server tokens skip automatic server login. Keep the whole PVC, including server/auth.enc, server configuration and .machine-id. A new Pod can reuse that login when it mounts the same data. With emptyDir, Pod replacement loses this data. Readiness does not prove that OAuth login succeeded.

The broker values example shows separate existing Secrets for downloader credentials and the broker bearer token. It deploys only the game server; deploy/authenticate the broker separately. Create the referenced Secrets in the server namespace. Secret values are never embedded in these examples. Do not put raw credentials in Helm env values.

items.title: Probes during downloads and updates
items.text:
Helm probes remain opt-in with probes.enabled=true. When enabled, the default is readiness only; startup and liveness probes are disabled. Kustomize's probes and production overlays use the same readiness-only policy.

A failed readiness check removes a Pod from Service endpoints without restarting it. Our check verifies server files, the process and UDP listener; it does not verify completed authentication or that a full world has loaded. A failed startup or liveness probe can restart the container. Therefore avoid restart probes during manual login, slow downloads and native in-process update handovers. The startup probe runs only at container startup, so extending it does not protect later updates.

For fully provisioned deployments you may explicitly enable startup/liveness probes and tune their thresholds. The optional startup default now allows 30 minutes (180 * 10s); choose a budget based on your actual environment. Keep liveness disabled for native updates unless you provide a check and budget that tolerate archive verification, backups and the Java restart.

Temporary extraction files are disk-backed emptyDir. Plan node ephemeral-storage capacity and limits for extracted server files; resources accepts Kubernetes requests/limits including ephemeral-storage. The download archive and assets live on /data. Using tmp.emptyDir.medium=Memory makes extraction count towards Pod memory usage, which can cause an OOM on constrained Pods.

items.title: Native Hytale updates on Kubernetes
items.text:
The native-update values example uses a 40Gi PVC, backups and readiness only:

env:
  HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD: "true"
  HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE: "false"
  HYTALE_NATIVE_UPDATES: "true"
  HYTALE_ENABLE_BACKUP: "true"
  HYTALE_BACKUP_ARCHIVE_MAX_COUNT: "3"
  ENABLE_AOT: "auto"

Use Hytale's direct OAuth login stored on the data volume. Broker session tokens alone cannot check for or download native updates. Keep the standard writable JAR/assets paths; do not mount individual server files read-only. The 40Gi example is a starting point, not a capacity guarantee: account for worlds, mods, staged assets, replacement copies and both server/update backups. Monitor free space.

kubectl exec <pod> -c hytale-server -- hytale-cli send "/update check"
kubectl exec <pod> -c hytale-server -- hytale-cli send "/update download"
# Check the logs and wait for the download to finish before applying:
kubectl exec <pod> -c hytale-server -- hytale-cli send "/update apply --confirm"
kubectl logs -f <pod> -c hytale-server

The container stays alive while its runner installs the staged package and starts Java again. Readiness may become false during this period. Keep enough termination grace for world saving and backups (the chart defaults to 120 seconds; measure your own workload). If an installation is interrupted, the runner recovers its recorded transaction on the next start. Do not manually remove that transaction directory. The file-replacement recovery does not undo world/config migrations after a new server has started. See the update and rollback guide.

Image upgrades and game updates are separate: select a new image tag through Helm or your Kustomize overlay. With native game updates enabled, set HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=false so startup downloads do not overwrite that installation.

items.title: Renew an expired downloader login
items.text:
Do not delete the PVC or the world directory. Downloader credentials are separate from server authentication. If a read-only credentials Secret is configured, replace it with a newly authenticated downloader credentials file, then recreate the Pod; that Secret is copied to /data on startup. subPath Secret mounts do not refresh in an existing container. Keep the Secret current as credentials rotate; otherwise an old file can overwrite the renewed on-volume credentials next start.

If the login exists only on /data, use the recovery Job. It uses the standard server file paths and may update the game files, so take a data backup first:

  1. Record the server's replica count and data PVC name. Scale its StatefulSet or Deployment to zero and wait for all server Pods to terminate. Suspend any GitOps reconciliation/autoscaling that would recreate them. This avoids concurrent writes, even on storage that permits multiple mounts.
  2. Copy renew-downloader-login.yaml and replace REPLACE_WITH_SERVER_DATA_PVC with that existing PVC. Use the same namespace and, if needed, node placement as the server volume. The Job uses the standard UID/GID 1000; mirror any custom data ownership settings from your server.
  3. Run the Job and follow its device login:
kubectl apply -f renew-downloader-login.yaml
kubectl logs -f job/hytale-renew-downloader-login
kubectl wait --for=condition=complete job/hytale-renew-downloader-login --timeout=3600s
  1. Only after successful completion, remove the Job and scale the server back to its recorded replica count. Resume reconciliation if you paused it.

The Job resets only downloader credentials and can download/update server files; it does not start Java or remove worlds/server credentials. It has no automatic retry loop and expires after completion. If it fails, inspect the logs before retrying; remove the failed Job before creating it again. Do not mount the old credentials Secret or combine credential seeding with reset mode.

items.title: Upgrading existing Helm installations and PVCs
items.text:
New claims default to 20Gi. This does not resize existing claims. Before an upgrade, save helm get values <release> --all and inspect the current StatefulSet volumeClaimTemplates and actual PVCs. Keep the existing template size in your values during the Helm upgrade (for example persistence.size=5Gi for an old installation); changing a StatefulSet claim template is rejected by Kubernetes. Do not use helm upgrade --force or delete data volumes to work around this. If your existing values enable startup/liveness probes, explicitly disable them for manual login or native updates; keeping old values also keeps their old probe settings. Choose the new readiness-only behavior deliberately.

If your StorageClass supports expansion, request a larger size on each existing PVC separately and wait for expansion to finish. Some storage drivers require a Pod restart for filesystem expansion. Back up the data before changes. The StatefulSet's original template can remain smaller while an existing PVC is larger; new replicas would still request the template size. Plan a separate controlled StatefulSet migration if you need a new template size. Existing-claim mode lets Helm reference a PVC managed outside the chart.

Persistent Deployment mode now uses Recreate, so a rollout stops the previous Pod before starting its replacement. This causes downtime but avoids normal rolling-update overlap against one world. It requires one replica. StatefulSets with an explicitly shared existingClaim also require one replica; StatefulSets with independent per-replica PVCs can still use multiple replicas. A PVC's ReadWriteOnce access mode alone does not prevent two Pods on one node from writing at once. During manual recovery or force deletion, wait for the previous process to stop before allowing any replacement to access the same volume.

The single-Pod Kustomize production PDB uses maxUnavailable: 0 and can block voluntary eviction during node drains. Plan downtime or adjust the budget during maintenance instead of force-deleting a running server.

Helm's NetworkPolicy, if enabled with its default empty egress rules, blocks outbound traffic. Configure DNS, HTTPS access for Hytale/downloads and access to your broker as needed. Kustomize's production policy currently allows all egress; tighten it for your environment without blocking authentication or updates.

items.title: What the manifest tests cover
items.text:
task k8s:test renders both workload kinds, published-package version overrides, first-start/native-update/broker values, existing and ephemeral volumes, secret references, replica guards and every Kustomize overlay (including probes). It checks Kubernetes schemas and specific safety properties, plus the recovery Job. Tools run in pinned Docker images by default. For installed Helm, Kustomize and kubeconform, use K8S_TEST_TOOLS=local sh ci/test-k8s-manifests.sh instead. Python 3 with venv/pip is required; the script installs pinned PyYAML in a temporary virtual environment and removes it afterwards.

These checks do not start a game server, sign in, mount a real PVC or validate storage-driver/network behavior in your cluster. Validate those with a separate test release and disposable data before updating production.

items.title: Kubernetes
items.text:
This repository ships optional Kubernetes deployment assets for the Docker image:

  • Docker Hub: hybrowse/hytale-server
  • GHCR: ghcr.io/hybrowse/hytale-server

The manifests are designed with:

  • secure defaults (non-root, minimal privileges)
  • operational flexibility (Helm values or Kustomize overlays)
  • no redistribution of proprietary Hytale server files

items.title: Helm
items.text: The Helm chart lives in deploy/helm/hytale-server. Published chart packages pin the image to the release version. The source chart currently targets image 1.2.0. ARM64 works without an architecture selector or privileged mode; only the official downloader uses emulation. Java remains native.

items.title: Add the Helm repo (GitHub Pages)
items.text:
After a release is published, the Helm repository is available at:

  • https://hybrowse.github.io/hytale-server-docker

Add it:

helm repo add hybrowse https://hybrowse.github.io/hytale-server-docker
helm repo update

items.title: Install with persistence (StatefulSet)
items.text:
Persistence is enabled by default in the Helm chart. You can tune the requested size; start with 20Gi and allow more for worlds, mods and backups. Native updates need room for staged files and recovery copies; the example uses 40Gi.

helm install hytale hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --set persistence.enabled=true \
  --set persistence.size=20Gi

Existing claims are not resized by changing this value alone. Read the upgrade notes below before upgrading an older installation.

items.title: Install (ephemeral /data, no PVC)
items.text:
For disposable testing only (all data is lost when the Pod is replaced):

helm install hytale hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --set persistence.enabled=false \
  --set env.HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true

Notes:

  • /data will be an emptyDir (lost when the Pod is replaced).
  • This is best suited for dev/testing or setups that synchronize state elsewhere.

items.title: Switch workload type to Deployment
items.text:
If you explicitly prefer a Deployment:

helm install hytale hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --set workload.kind=Deployment

If you want persistence with Deployment mode, the chart creates a PVC unless you point it at an existing one:

helm install hytale hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --set workload.kind=Deployment \
  --set persistence.enabled=true \
  --set persistence.existingClaim=my-existing-claim

items.title: Exposing the UDP port
items.text:
By default, the chart creates a ClusterIP Service (internal).

For external exposure, options depend on your cluster:

  • service.type=LoadBalancer (common on managed clusters)
  • service.type=NodePort (requires firewall / node routing)

Examples:

helm install hytale hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --set service.type=LoadBalancer

helm install hytale hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --set service.type=NodePort \
  --set service.nodePort=30520

items.title: Example: values.yaml snippet (persistence and environment variables)
items.text:
If you prefer a values file over long --set commands, use this starting point. Broker integration is optional; enable it only after deploying and authenticating a broker.

workload:
  kind: StatefulSet

persistence:
  enabled: true
  size: 20Gi

env:
  HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD: "true"
  HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE: "true"

  # Optional (advanced): fetch server session/identity tokens from the Hytale Session Token Broker by Hybrowse
  # and skip the interactive /auth flow.
  # HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_ENABLED: "true"
  # HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_URL: "http://hytale-session-token-broker:8080"

If your broker uses an HTTP bearer token, prefer mounting it as a file and set HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_BEARER_TOKEN_SRC. You can do this via extraVolumes / extraVolumeMounts and env.

items.title: Example: wiring secrets (server auth, CurseForge, downloader credentials)
items.text:
The chart supports referencing existing Kubernetes Secret objects via .Values.secrets.*. This avoids putting secrets into Helm values files.

Example secrets (create once per environment):

apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: hytale-server-auth
type: Opaque
stringData:
  sessionToken: "<redacted>"
  identityToken: "<redacted>"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: hytale-curseforge
type: Opaque
stringData:
  apiKey: "<redacted>"
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Secret
metadata:
  name: hytale-downloader-credentials
type: Opaque
stringData:
  credentials.json: "{...}"

Then reference them from Helm values:

secrets:
  serverAuth:
    name: hytale-server-auth
    sessionTokenKey: sessionToken
    identityTokenKey: identityToken

  curseforge:
    name: hytale-curseforge
    apiKeyKey: apiKey

  downloaderCredentials:
    name: hytale-downloader-credentials
    credentialsKey: credentials.json

Notes:

  • The chart maps server auth secrets to HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN / HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN.
  • The chart mounts the CurseForge key and downloader credentials as files and sets HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY_SRC / HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC.

items.title: Production pattern: multi-environment and multi-region
items.text: Treat each region as a separate Helm release. Keep its configuration, credentials and persistent data separate from other environments.

items.title: Namespaces
items.text: Use one namespace per environment, such as hytale-dev, hytale-staging and hytale-prod. For multiple regions, use names such as hytale-prod-eu and hytale-prod-us.

items.title: Values files
items.text:
Keep non-secret configuration in values files and apply regional overrides after the shared configuration:

File Purpose values.prod.yaml Shared production settings values.prod-eu.yaml Overrides for the EU deployment values.prod-us.yaml Overrides for the US deployment

Use separate files such as values.dev.yaml and values.staging.yaml for other environments. Do not put credentials in these files.

items.title: Secrets and permissions
items.text:
Create Kubernetes Secrets separately in each namespace, preferably through your existing secret manager or GitOps tooling. Consistent Secret names let you reuse the same values structure across environments.

After rotating credentials, recreate the affected Pods so they read the updated values. Environment variables and subPath Secret mounts do not refresh inside an existing container.

Keep serviceAccount.automount=false unless the server needs Kubernetes API access. Give external secret tooling access only to the namespaces it manages.

items.title: Release names
items.text:
Choose explicit names such as hytale-eu and hytale-us. For example, after preparing the values files and Secrets:

helm install hytale-eu hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --namespace hytale-prod-eu --create-namespace \
  -f values.prod.yaml -f values.prod-eu.yaml
helm install hytale-us hybrowse/hytale-server \
  --namespace hytale-prod-us --create-namespace \
  -f values.prod.yaml -f values.prod-us.yaml

items.title: Operations
items.text: See Kubernetes operations for first login, probes, native updates, credential recovery and existing PVCs.

items.title: Kustomize
items.text: See the Kustomize guide.

items.title: Validation
items.text:
Locally you can validate that the Kubernetes manifests render and pass schema validation:

task k8s:test

items.title: Kustomize
items.text:
Choose an overlay deliberately: the base and development overlay use disposable data, while production adds persistence and network restrictions.

Kustomize manifests live in deploy/kustomize.

items.title: Base
items.text:
deploy/kustomize/base is intentionally minimal and uses an emptyDir for /data.

kustomize build deploy/kustomize/base | kubectl apply -f -

Alternatively, if you prefer using kubectl's built-in kustomize support:

kubectl kustomize deploy/kustomize/base | kubectl apply -f -

The base pins image hybrowse/hytale-server:1.2.0. To select a different image, use an images override in your own overlay; do not rely on cached latest tags. The development overlay uses Always, but still resolves the pinned version. Temporary extraction files use disk-backed emptyDir, not RAM. Account for node ephemeral-storage capacity as well as PVC space.

items.title: Overlays
items.text:
• deploy/kustomize/overlays/development: enables auto-download and uses imagePullPolicy: Always
  • deploy/kustomize/overlays/production: enables a 20Gi PVC, PDB, NetworkPolicy, backups and readiness checks
  • deploy/kustomize/overlays/probes: readiness checks without startup/liveness restart deadlines
kustomize build deploy/kustomize/overlays/development | kubectl apply -f -

With kubectl:

kubectl kustomize deploy/kustomize/overlays/development | kubectl apply -f -

kustomize build deploy/kustomize/overlays/production | kubectl apply -f -

With kubectl:

kubectl kustomize deploy/kustomize/overlays/production | kubectl apply -f -

items.title: Validation
items.text:
Locally you can validate that the Kubernetes manifests render and pass schema validation:

task k8s:test

Read Kubernetes operations for login, updates, probes and PVC migrations.

items.title: Networking and player connections
items.text: Hytale uses QUIC over UDP. The default listen address is 0.0.0.0:5520 inside the container.

items.title: Change the public port
items.text:
To expose UDP 15520 on the Docker host while leaving the server's internal port unchanged:

services:
  hytale:
    ports:
      - "15520:5520/udp"

Players connect to the host on port 15520. HYTALE_BIND controls the address inside the container, not Docker's published host port. Usually it should remain 0.0.0.0:5520; binding to 127.0.0.1 inside the container prevents normal outside connections.

items.title: Check the connection in order
items.text:
1. Confirm server login succeeded in the logs. Downloader authorization alone is insufficient.
  2. Try a direct connection from the Docker host using the published port.
  3. Try the host's LAN address from another computer.
  4. For internet access, check the router's UDP forwarding, host firewall and any provider firewall/security group.
  5. Test from another network to avoid relying on router NAT-loopback behavior.

A socket or successful transport probe is not a complete Hytale login test. Doctor deliberately reports external connectivity as unknown.

items.title: Kubernetes
items.text: A ClusterIP Service is internal. Expose UDP with a compatible LoadBalancer or NodePort and configure the surrounding network accordingly. See Kubernetes setup.

items.title: Hyrouter
items.text: Hyrouter refers players to a backend; it does not tunnel gameplay traffic. The client must reach both the router and the selected backend. See router integration.

items.title: Download worlds and mods before startup
items.text:
On startup, this image can optionally download additional content into the server data directories before starting the Java process.

Supported targets:

  • universe/ (world + player save data)
  • mods/

The download list is a space/comma/newline-separated list of http:// / https:// URLs. Each list item can also be a reference to a file by prefixing it with @. The file is read line-by-line; empty lines and # comments are ignored.

Each URL is downloaded at most once per /data volume by default (a marker file is stored under /data/.hytale-prestart-downloads/). To re-download, use the *_FORCE=true option.

Downloaded files:

  • If the downloaded payload is a ZIP archive, it is extracted into the destination directory.
  • Otherwise the payload is saved as a file in the destination directory.

Optional throttling:

  • *_LIMIT_RATE maps to curl --limit-rate (for example 500k, 2m).

Security notes:

  • The image does not log URL query strings and redacts URL userinfo (for example https://user:pass@...).
  • Only http(s) is supported.

items.title: Example (download a universe and mods)
items.text:
services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      HYTALE_UNIVERSE_DOWNLOAD_URLS: "https://example.com/my-universe.zip"
      HYTALE_UNIVERSE_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT_RATE: "5m"

      HYTALE_MODS_DOWNLOAD_URLS: "@/data/mods-urls.txt"
      HYTALE_MODS_DOWNLOAD_LIMIT_RATE: "2m"

Multiline example:

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      HYTALE_UNIVERSE_DOWNLOAD_URLS: |
        https://example.com/a.zip
        https://example.com/b.zip
      HYTALE_MODS_DOWNLOAD_URLS: |
        https://example.com/mod1.zip, https://example.com/mod2.zip
        https://example.com/mod3.zip

These are additions to your service definition, not standalone Compose files. Take an existing world offline and preserve a backup before forcing downloads into its data directory.

items.title: Start a server with Docker Compose
items.text: This guide starts one server, stores its data in a Docker volume and walks through both first-time logins. You need Docker with Compose and a Hytale account that can authorize a dedicated server.

items.title: 1. Create the service
items.text:
Save this complete example as compose.yaml in an empty directory:

services:
  hytale:
    image: hybrowse/hytale-server:latest
    environment:
      HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD: "true"
    ports:
      - "5520:5520/udp"
    volumes:
      - hytale-data:/data
    stop_grace_period: 120s
    restart: unless-stopped

volumes:
  hytale-data:

The named volume avoids host-directory ownership problems on first startup. To use a bind mount instead, follow data and permissions. For production, replace latest with a specific published image tag.

Start the container and watch its logs:

docker compose up -d
docker compose logs -f hytale

On AMD64 and ARM64, use the native image. Do not add platform: linux/amd64 on Apple Silicon. You do not need privileged mode, a terminal attachment or a local Java installation.

items.title: 2. Authorize the downloader
items.text:
Open the authorization URL printed in the logs and confirm the displayed code. The official downloader obtains the server files and assets. This can take several minutes and needs several gigabytes of free storage.

Downloader credentials are saved on /data and reused on later starts. They are independent of the server login in the next step.

If downloading stops with invalid_grant, use downloader login recovery. If you already have the official files, use manual provisioning instead.

items.title: 3. Authorize the running server
items.text:
After the download, Java starts and the image automatically requests Hytale's device login with encrypted persistence. Follow this second authorization URL in the logs.

If your account has several profiles, select one using the name or number Hytale displays:

docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli auth select ExamplePlayer

Request live authentication status, then read the result in the logs:

docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli auth status
docker compose logs --tail 50 hytale

Look for Hytale's authentication-success message. A running container or a healthy probe alone does not establish that players can join.

The login, selected profile and machine identity remain on the data volume. Do not delete the volume to resolve a downloader error. For manual login or automated fleets, see authentication.

items.title: 4. Connect
items.text:
In Hytale Direct Connect, enter the Docker host's address and port 5520. When the client runs on the same host, use 127.0.0.1:5520. For another computer, use the host's reachable LAN or public address.

For internet access, forward UDP 5520 to the Docker host and allow it in the host firewall. Forwarding TCP alone is insufficient. See networking if local connections work but remote ones fail.

items.title: 5. Stop and restart safely
items.text:
docker compose stop hytale
docker compose up -d hytale

The same volume is reused, so normal restarts should not need a new login. docker compose down also retains the named volume; docker compose down --volumes deletes it and its server data.

items.title: Next steps
items.text:
• Configure server name, player limit and JSON files.
  • Set memory limits and heap size.
  • Install CurseForge mods.
  • Choose an update method.
  • Run Doctor for read-only checks and support reports.

items.title: Java, memory and AOT
items.text: The official Hytale server requires Java 25. This image uses Adoptium / Eclipse Temurin 25, with a minimum runtime version of 25.0.5 (eclipse-temurin:25-jre-noble, pinned to a digest). While the official Docker image is still on 25.0.4.1, the build installs the official 25.0.5 JRE archive for AMD64 or ARM64 and verifies its SHA-256 checksum. Newer runtimes in the base image are kept. Use java -version inside the container to check the installed runtime.

items.title: Heap sizing
items.text:
If JVM_XMS / JVM_XMX are not set, the JVM will pick defaults (based on available container memory). This is usually fine for testing, but for predictable production operation you should set at least JVM_XMX to an explicit limit. There are no universal best-practice values; monitor RAM/CPU usage for your player count and playstyle and experiment with different values. If you see high CPU usage from garbage collection, that can be a symptom of memory pressure and an JVM_XMX value that is too low. In that case, try increasing JVM_XMX (or reducing view distance / workload) and compare behavior.

You can optionally set JVM_XMS as well. Keeping JVM_XMS lower than JVM_XMX allows the heap to grow as needed. Setting JVM_XMS equal to JVM_XMX can reduce heap resizing overhead but increases baseline memory usage.

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      JVM_XMS: "2G"
      JVM_XMX: "6G"

Leave memory outside the heap for threads, native libraries and filesystem cache. A 6G heap needs a container limit larger than 6G. Doctor checks explicit heap settings against detected cgroup limits.

items.title: AOT cache
items.text:
Hytale ships with a pre-trained AOT cache (HytaleServer.aot), but AOT caches require a compatible Java runtime. If you see AOT cache errors during startup, generate a cache that matches the Java version/build inside the container.

AOT caches are also architecture-specific (e.g. linux/amd64 vs linux/arm64). If you switch the container platform (or move the /data volume between machines), delete and regenerate the cache. If the cache is incompatible (for example shipped for a different architecture), ENABLE_AOT=auto should ignore it and continue startup. For strict diagnostics, use ENABLE_AOT=true (fails fast). For normal operation, prefer ENABLE_AOT=auto.

  • ENABLE_AOT=auto (default): enables AOT only when the cache file exists.
  • ENABLE_AOT=true: requires the cache file to exist and fails fast otherwise.
  • ENABLE_AOT=false: do not use AOT.
  • ENABLE_AOT=generate: generates an AOT cache at HYTALE_AOT_PATH, then exits.

If you see Java warnings about restricted native access (e.g. Netty), you can set:

  • JVM_EXTRA_ARGS=--enable-native-access=ALL-UNNAMED

items.title: Machine identity
items.text:
The Hytale server reads /etc/machine-id to generate a stable hardware UUID. In Docker containers, this file is typically missing or read-only. This image automatically generates a stable machine ID and persists it in /data/.machine-id.

The machine ID is used by the Hytale server to encrypt the auth.enc file (which stores authentication credentials from /auth login device). This image replicates the standard Linux behavior where /etc/machine-id is readable by all processes.

You can override the auto-generated machine ID:

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      HYTALE_MACHINE_ID: "0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef"

The value must be exactly 32 lowercase hexadecimal characters (no dashes).

items.title: Security
items.text: This document describes security hardening recommendations for running the hybrowse/hytale-server image.

items.title: Guiding principles
items.text:
• Run as non-root (this image uses UID 1000 by default).
  • Treat authentication material as secrets.
  • Prefer least-privilege runtime settings.
  • Avoid changes that accidentally redistribute proprietary server assets.

For legal/policy notes (unofficial status, no redistribution, and operator responsibilities), see the repository README.md.

items.title: Secrets
items.text:
Treat these as secrets and avoid placing them in plain text config repositories:

  • /data/.hytale-downloader-credentials.json
  • HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN
  • HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN
  • HYTALE_AUTH_KEY / the contents of HYTALE_AUTH_KEY_FILE
  • HYTALE_SERVER_OFFLINE_TOKEN
  • HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_BEARER_TOKEN
  • CurseForge API key (HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_API_KEY)

Recommendations:

  • Prefer file-based secrets when possible (for example *_SRC style variables).
  • In Docker Compose, use secrets: and mount them read-only.
  • In Kubernetes, use Secret objects and mount them as files.

items.title: Recommended baseline
items.text:
• Keep the container running as the default non-root user.
  • Avoid --privileged.
  • Do not add extra Linux capabilities unless you have a specific need.

items.title: Read-only root filesystem (optional)
items.text:
read_only / readOnlyRootFilesystem can cause issues with the official server's hardware UUID detection. In particular, if the container cannot write /etc/machine-id, the server may fail with Failed to get Hardware UUID.

For this reason, a read-only root filesystem is not recommended by default. If you still enable it, ensure you have a working machine-id strategy and writable mounts:

  • Provide a writable /tmp (tmpfs) for temporary files.
  • Ensure /data is writable (this image persists a stable machine-id under /data).

Example (Compose):

services:
  hytale:
    read_only: true
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp
    volumes:
      - ./data:/data

items.title: Drop privileges and prevent escalation
items.text:
Example (Compose):

services:
  hytale:
    security_opt:
      - no-new-privileges:true

If your runtime supports it, also consider:

  • cap_drop: ["ALL"]

items.title: Pod security
items.text:
Recommended settings:

  • runAsNonRoot: true
  • allowPrivilegeEscalation: false
  • capabilities.drop: ["ALL"]

items.title: Read-only root filesystem (optional)
items.text: readOnlyRootFilesystem: true is not recommended by default due to the machine-id / hardware UUID behavior described above. If you enable it, you should typically also provide an emptyDir mount for /tmp and ensure /data remains writable.

items.title: NetworkPolicy
items.text:
If you deploy into a cluster with NetworkPolicies enforced, restrict:

  • Ingress to UDP 5520
  • Egress to what you need

Notes:

  • If you use HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, the container must be able to reach the official Hytale downloader endpoints.
  • If you use CurseForge mods, the container must be able to reach the CurseForge API and download endpoints.

items.title: Resource limits
items.text: Set CPU/memory requests and limits to reduce noisy-neighbor effects and to make restarts/evictions more predictable.

items.title: Termination behavior
items.text: The server is expected to stop cleanly on SIGTERM. For recommended grace periods, see upgrades.md.

items.title: Server files (manual provisioning)
items.text:
Note

You usually don't need this page. The quickstart enables HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, so the container downloads and provisions server files automatically.

Manual provisioning is needed if:

  • You prefer to provision files yourself instead of running the downloader (available on AMD64 and ARM64)
  • You want to pin a specific server version
  • You prefer full control over file provisioning

This Docker image runs the official Hytale dedicated server binaries from a mounted volume. This repository and image do not redistribute proprietary Hytale server binaries or assets.

You are responsible for obtaining the required files via official channels and for complying with the Hytale EULA, Terms of Service, and Server Operator Policies: https://hytale.com/server-policies

You must provide these files yourself:

  • Assets.zip
  • the Server/ folder contents (at minimum HytaleServer.jar, plus additional runtime files)

items.title: Option A: Official Hytale Downloader (recommended)
items.text:
The official docs provide the downloader archive here:

  • https://downloader.hytale.com/hytale-downloader.zip

Typical flow:

  1. Download and extract the archive.
  2. Run the downloader and store the game package zip:
./hytale-downloader -download-path game.zip
  1. Extract required artifacts from game.zip:
unzip -o game.zip 'Assets.zip'
unzip -o game.zip 'Server/*' -d .

You should now have:

  • ./Assets.zip
  • ./Server/ (folder)

items.title: Option B: Copy from Hytale launcher installation
items.text:
If you have the game installed via the launcher, the official manual documents a directory containing a Server/ folder and Assets.zip.

Documented paths:

  • Windows: %appdata%\Hytale\install\release\package\game\latest
  • Linux: $XDG_DATA_HOME/Hytale/install/release/package/game/latest
  • macOS: ~/Library/Application Support/Hytale/install/release/package/game/latest

Copy both artifacts (keep them as a matched set when updating):

  • Assets.zip
  • Server/ (entire folder)

items.title: Provide the files to the container
items.text:
Expected volume layout:

  • ./data/Assets.zip
  • ./data/server/ (contents of Server/)

Example:

./data/
  Assets.zip
  server/
    HytaleServer.jar
    ...

If you extracted via Option A, you can provision like this:

mkdir -p ./data/server
cp -f ./Assets.zip ./data/Assets.zip
cp -a ./Server/. ./data/server/

Then start the container:

docker compose up -d

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• Keep Assets.zip and Server/ in sync when updating.
  • Avoid committing these files to source control.

items.title: Startup order
items.text:
The startup sequence is fixed and relevant when combining auto-download and token broker:

  1. Validate required files (/data/Assets.zip, /data/server/HytaleServer.jar) and run auto-download/update if enabled.
  2. Install/update CurseForge mods (if configured).
  3. Run pre-start universe/mod downloads (if configured).
  4. Ensure /data/server/config.json exists and apply HYTALE_CONFIG_* patches.
  5. Apply CFG_* interpolation.
  6. Run Session Token Broker (if enabled and tokens are not already set).
  7. Start the Java server process.

This means: if an earlier step fails or blocks (for example downloader auth on first run), the Session Token Broker step is not reached yet.

  1. On a fresh authenticated server, queue Hytale device login if automatic login is enabled.

See authentication for the separate downloader and server logins.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text:
Common issues and how to fix them.

Start with docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli doctor for read-only checks. For a shareable JSON report, use hytale-cli report. See diagnostics for coverage, privacy, exit codes and optional network checks.

Warning

This is the most common issue. If players can't connect, check this first.

items.title: Server authentication error: "Server authentication unavailable"
items.text:
Symptom: Players cannot connect; you see this in server logs:

[SEVERE] [HandshakeHandler] Server session token not available - cannot request auth grant
[INFO] [Hytale] Disconnecting ... with the message: Server authentication unavailable - please try again later

Cause: The server is not authenticated. In HYTALE_AUTH_MODE=authenticated (the default), the server must complete a device-code login after startup before players can connect.

Fix:

For a fresh server, first check the logs for the automatically started device login. To start a new login with encrypted persistence:

docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli auth login

If several profiles are offered, use hytale-cli auth select <name-or-number>. For manual console access:

  1. Attach to the server console:
docker compose attach hytale
  1. Run:
/auth login device

  1. Follow the URL + device code shown in the console.

  2. If multiple profiles are shown, pick one:

/auth select <number>
  1. Check status:
/auth status

Detach without stopping the server:

  • Press Ctrl-p then Ctrl-q

items.title: Downloader authentication (first-time setup)
items.text:
Symptom: Container logs show a URL + device code on first run.

Cause: The official Hytale Downloader uses OAuth device-code flow to authenticate before downloading server files.

Fix: Open the URL in your browser and enter the device code shown in the logs. After completion, the download will proceed.

Watch logs during first-time auth:

docker compose logs -f hytale

Note

ARM64 images include emulation for the official downloader. Java and the game server remain native; no platform: linux/amd64 override is needed.

items.title: Expired downloader login (invalid_grant)
items.text:
If auto-download stops with oauth2: "invalid_grant", the saved downloader login has expired or been revoked. This happens before the game server starts, so changing HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS does not help.

For Docker Compose, sign in once using a temporary container:

docker compose stop hytale
docker compose run --rm --no-deps \
  -e HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true \
  -e HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=true \
  -e HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_RESET_CREDENTIALS=true \
  --entrypoint /usr/local/bin/hytale-auto-download hytale
docker compose up -d hytale

Follow the device-login URL in the temporary container's output. The regular container then reuses the new login. Worlds, configuration and server authentication are preserved. Keep the same volumes and platform as the regular service.

If HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC is set, obtain a fresh downloader login and replace that mounted file instead. Otherwise the old login would be copied back on every start. Resetting and seeding credentials together is rejected.

On other platforms, set HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_RESET_CREDENTIALS=true for one startup, follow the login in the logs, then remove the setting before restarting again.

items.title: Session Token Broker enabled, but no broker logs
items.text:
Symptom: HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_ENABLED=true is set, but startup logs show no broker activity.

Cause: The broker step runs later in startup. If an earlier phase fails or blocks, broker logs will not appear yet. Common examples:

  • Auto-download/update is still waiting on first-time downloader device auth.
  • Auto-download failed before startup reached the broker step.
  • Both HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN and HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN are already set (broker is skipped by design).

Fix:

  • Check full container logs from startup (docker compose logs -f hytale), not only interactive attach output.
  • For non-interactive startup, either:
    • seed /data/.hytale-downloader-credentials.json via HYTALE_DOWNLOADER_CREDENTIALS_SRC, or
    • pre-provision /data/Assets.zip and /data/server/HytaleServer.jar and set HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=false.

items.title: Auto-download on ARM64 (Apple Silicon)
items.text:
Current ARM64 images run the official x86-64 downloader through a bundled emulator. Java and the game server run natively. No privileged mode or host emulation setup is required.

If you see the old error Auto-download is not supported on arm64, update the image and recreate the container:

docker compose pull hytale
docker compose up -d hytale

Remove any platform: linux/amd64 override from your Compose service to use the native ARM64 image. Keep the existing /data volume so downloaded files, worlds and credentials are preserved. Follow any downloader login prompt in the logs.

Manual provisioning remains available: server-files.md.

items.title: Permission denied errors on /data
items.text:
Symptom:

cp: cannot create regular file '/data/server/./HytaleServer.jar': Permission denied

Cause: The container runs as uid=1000 (non-root) by default. If the host directory mounted to /data is owned by a different user, the container cannot write to it.

Fix: Make the host directory writable for uid 1000:

sudo chown -R 1000:1000 /path/to/your/data

Or, if you want to use a different uid, run the container with a matching user:

services:
  hytale:
    user: "1001:1001"

Warning

Avoid running as root (user: "0:0") in production.

items.title: Read-only root filesystem
items.text:
Symptom: When running with a read-only root filesystem (e.g., Kubernetes with readOnlyRootFilesystem: true):

WARNING: Could not write to /etc/machine-id (read-only filesystem?)
WARNING: The Hytale server may fail with 'Failed to get Hardware UUID'.

Cause: The container needs to write a machine-id to /etc/machine-id. The Hytale server reads this file for hardware identification.

Fix (Kubernetes): Disable read-only root filesystem:

securityContext:
  readOnlyRootFilesystem: false

The machine-id is persisted to /data/.machine-id for stability across restarts.

Fix (Docker Compose): Mount /tmp as tmpfs if needed:

services:
  hytale:
    volumes:
      - /path/to/data:/data
    tmpfs:
      - /tmp

items.title: Container exits immediately with "Missing server jar" or "Missing assets"
items.text:
Symptom: Container exits with clear error messages about missing files.

Cause: The server files and Assets.zip are not present in /data.

Fix:

  • Set HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true to let the container download them automatically.
  • Or provision files manually: server-files.md

Tip

AOT errors are usually harmless with ENABLE_AOT=auto (default). The server will continue without AOT.

items.title: AOT cache errors on startup
items.text:
Symptom: Java errors mentioning AOT cache incompatibility or "modules size has changed".

Cause: The AOT cache was generated for a different Java version or architecture.

Fix:

  • Delete the existing cache (./data/server/HytaleServer.aot) and regenerate it, or
  • Set ENABLE_AOT=false to disable AOT.

See: configuration.md

items.title: High CPU usage from garbage collection
items.text:
Symptom: Server uses a lot of CPU even with few players; GC logs show frequent collections.

Cause: The JVM heap is too small for the workload.

Fix: Increase JVM_XMX:

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      JVM_XMX: "6G"

Monitor and experiment with different values.

See: configuration.md

items.title: CurseForge mods: HTTP 403 when resolving download URL
items.text:
Symptom: You see a warning like:

WARNING: failed to install mod <modId>: failed to resolve download URL (CurseForge API returned HTTP 403 ...)

Cause: CurseForge returned HTTP 403 for the download-url endpoint. This often means the mod author has disabled third-party/API downloads for the project.

Fix:

  • Remove the mod from HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_MODS.
  • If the mod is essential, ask the author to enable API downloads or install the mod manually.

Debug: Set HYTALE_CURSEFORGE_DEBUG=true to print additional diagnostics on API failures.

items.title: Upgrades
items.text:
This document describes how to upgrade the hybrowse/hytale-server Docker image safely.

Image updates and game updates are separate. Choose who manages game files:

Method Settings When files change Startup downloader HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=true Before Java starts, when a new game version is found Provision only HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true, HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=false Only when required files are missing Native Hytale updater HYTALE_NATIVE_UPDATES=true, HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=false After an authorized in-game update Manual provisioning HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=false When you replace the matched game files yourself

items.title: General upgrade guidance
items.text:
• Prefer pinning a specific image tag (for example hybrowse/hytale-server:1.2.1) instead of using latest.
  • Always persist /data if you expect your server files, universe, mods, auth state, and backups to survive restarts.
  • Consider taking an out-of-band backup (for example a snapshot of the /data volume) before upgrading.

items.title: Graceful shutdown: recommended grace periods
items.text:
The Hytale dedicated server typically stops and flushes state quickly. Allow time for world saving, mods and backups; measure your own shutdown time rather than relying on a universal timeout.

  • Docker Compose: stop_grace_period: 120s
  • Kubernetes: terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120

If your host is under heavy load, or you run large universes/modpacks, increase this further if shutdown does not finish within the configured grace period.

items.title: Docker Compose upgrade
items.text:
Typical upgrade flow:

  1. Ensure your ./data:/data volume mount is persistent.

  2. Stop the container (gracefully):

    • docker compose down

  3. Pull the new image:

    • docker compose pull

  4. Start again:

    • docker compose up -d

items.title: Note: server file updates
items.text:
There are two common models:

  • If you use HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true:

    • With HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=true (default), the container checks for updates on each start and downloads new server files into /data when an update is available.
    • With HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=false, downloads happen only when files are missing.

  • If you provision server files manually:

    • Replace /data/server/HytaleServer.jar and /data/Assets.zip out-of-band.
    • This project must not redistribute proprietary server files.

items.title: Helm
items.text:
• Prefer pinning the chart/app version and the image tag.
  • Upgrade by changing the image tag and running helm upgrade.

Recommended termination grace period:

  • terminationGracePeriodSeconds: 120

items.title: Kustomize
items.text: • Change the image tag in your overlay and apply.

items.title: Notes
items.text:
• If you use a PVC for /data, upgrades should preserve world state and authentication as long as you keep the PVC.
  • If you run with ephemeral /data (emptyDir), upgrades will naturally discard state on restart.

items.title: Downgrades / rollbacks
items.text: Rolling back the image tag is possible, but rolling back server files and world state may not be safe. If you need reliable rollbacks, use snapshots/backups of /data and restore those in addition to changing the image tag.

items.title: In-game server updates
items.text:
Opt in with:

environment:
  HYTALE_NATIVE_UPDATES: "true"
  HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE: "false"
  HYTALE_ENABLE_BACKUP: "true"

Remove HYTALE_DISABLE_UPDATES=true if previously set. HYTALE_AUTO_DOWNLOAD=true can still provision missing files on first startup, but its startup update check must be disabled so that two mechanisms do not update the same installation.

Hytale needs a direct server OAuth login to check for and download updates. Use /auth persistence Encrypted and /auth login device once, and keep the credential store in /data. Broker-provided session/identity tokens authenticate players but do not provide the OAuth refresh token needed by the built-in updater. With broker-only authentication, use the startup downloader for downloads instead. The image can still install an already staged package and restart with broker tokens.

Send the normal Hytale update commands, checking the server logs between steps:

docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli send "/update check"
docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli send "/update download"
# Wait for the download to finish, then:
docker compose exec hytale hytale-cli send "/update apply --confirm"

Hytale performs its configured pre-update backups, shuts down with exit code 8, and the image then verifies and installs the staged files before restarting Java. A staged update is also applied at the next container start, matching the official launcher workflow. A crash or a regular shutdown does not trigger an internal restart. An update exit without staged files fails with a clear error instead of looping.

Use the standard /data/server/HytaleServer.jar, /data/Assets.zip and AOT paths. The files and their directories must be writable; mount the /data volume rather than individual read-only JAR/assets files. Only one update runner can hold the volume lock at a time. No root privileges are required.

items.title: What is replaced
items.text:
A complete staged package must contain both the JAR and Assets.zip; partial or JAR-only packages are rejected. Only those files, optional AOT input configuration and the license directory are installed. Staged launcher scripts, configuration, mods and authentication files are not executed or installed. World data and credentials stay in place. The existing AOT cache is removed because it may not match the new server. Use ENABLE_AOT=auto or false for unattended updates; strict mode needs a matching cache to be generated again before the next start.

The image checks archive integrity and rejects staged links or special files. It prepares the replacement files and records the previous binaries before changing live files. A failed install restores the previous files. An interrupted transaction is recovered before Java can start. Keep enough free disk space for the staged package, prepared replacements and backups.

Previous binaries are retained at /data/updater/image-backup/previous/: jar, assets, aotconfig, aot and licenses correspond to their managed paths. Hytale's own /data/updater/backup is separate and is left untouched. Once the new server has started, the image does not roll it back automatically: world or config migrations may already have happened. A version rollback should include a compatible world/config snapshot, as described above.

If validation fails, the live files stay unchanged. Inspect the log and staged package, cancel the incomplete update with Hytale's /update cancel while native update mode is disabled if necessary, then download it again. Do not delete image-transaction while recovering an interrupted install.

items.title: Hytale compatibility
items.text: The documented server options were checked against the actual 0.7.4 server's --help. If either removed environment option is enabled, the image stops before Java starts and explains its replacement. Ignoring broken mods is an explicit recovery choice, not the same operation as skipping validation. Schema exports need an output path writable by UID 1000; use a directory under /data.

items.title: Native server environment variables
items.text:
Docker passes these directly to Hytale; no EXTRA_SERVER_ARGS mapping is needed:

Variable Purpose HYTALE_AUTH_KEY_FILE File containing the passphrase for Hytale's encrypted credential store. Mount it read-only and keep the same secret across restarts. HYTALE_AUTH_KEY Inline alternative to the key file. Treat it as a secret; prefer the file option. HYTALE_DISABLE_UPDATES Disable Hytale's built-in updater. This is separate from this image's HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE, which runs the downloader before startup.

The key variables apply to Hytale's own encrypted credential store, not to the broker's storage or the downloader credentials. Both are already separate flows. When managing updates through the image/downloader, set HYTALE_DISABLE_UPDATES=true. To use Hytale's own /update download and /update apply --confirm flow, set HYTALE_NATIVE_UPDATES=true and HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE=false; do not set HYTALE_DISABLE_UPDATES=true. See upgrades.md.

The server also reads HYTALE_SERVER_OFFLINE_TOKEN and HYTALE_SERVER_AUDIENCE. These are advanced authentication inputs, not replacements for the documented broker session/identity token flow. No image default is assigned to either.

items.title: Upcoming Update 8 changes (pre-release)
items.text:
Update 8 pre-release notes announce quiche as the dedicated server default. Existing HYTALE_TRANSPORT=QUIC selects the Netty fallback; leaving it empty preserves the server's own default. Linux ARM64 falls back when a quiche native library is unavailable. This has not been tested against a pre-release server here; the current 0.7.4 test uses Netty.

The notes also describe SentryDsn in config.json; the actual 0.7.4 config schema already exposes this field. Supply it through HYTALE_CONFIG_PATCH_JSON (or its _SRC file option), without another image variable. HYTALE_DISABLE_SENTRY=true still disables reporting. The notes describe a world-event save migration to universe/resources/GlobalWorldEvents.json; preserve the entire /data volume and make a backup before upgrading or rolling back.

The Update 7 notes add a guard against writing into the launcher installation directory. The image's writable paths are under /data, so it does not need to bypass that guard with --allow-install-dir. The new --bootstrap flow is not integrated: the image's normal file checks and downloader remain the supported installation flow.

Find settings by task. Each reference lists defaults and accepted values; the guides show complete workflows.

Image behavior and game-server behavior are separate. For example HYTALE_AUTO_UPDATE controls the startup downloader, while HYTALE_DISABLE_UPDATES is read directly by Hytale.

items.title: Hybrowse server stack
items.text:
A single server only needs the game-server image. The broker and router address different needs and can be added independently.

Component Use it when Owns Hytale server image You want to run the game server Worlds, mods, configuration, game files and server login Session Token Broker Servers need centrally managed, non-interactive authentication Long-lived OAuth state and short-lived session minting Hyrouter Players should be referred to a selected backend Routing rules and referral decisions

items.title: Connection and authentication flow
items.text:
1. A game server obtains its files through the downloader or manual provisioning.
  2. It authenticates directly with Hytale, or obtains short-lived session/identity tokens from a broker at startup.
  3. A client connects directly to a game server, or first visits Hyrouter and receives a backend referral.
  4. After referral, the client connects to that backend itself.

The broker does not download game files. Hyrouter does not replace the game server's authentication or relay gameplay packets. Keep each component's credentials, persistence and network exposure separate.

See startup order when a configured component appears not to be called.

items.title: Session Token Broker integration
items.text:
If you run the Hytale Session Token Broker by Hybrowse, this image can fetch session_token and identity_token from it at container startup and pass them to the server process.

When both HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN and HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN are already set, the broker is skipped.

This is primarily intended for providers / fleets / networks that want non-interactive authentication without attaching to the server console. The reference broker implementation by Hybrowse lives here: Hytale Session Token Broker

How credentials are used:

  • The broker persists long-lived OAuth state (refresh token) and mints short-lived game session tokens on demand.
  • This image only sees the short-lived HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN / HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN at startup and passes them to the Java process through its environment, keeping them out of process arguments.

Security notes:

  • Treat HYTALE_SERVER_SESSION_TOKEN, HYTALE_SERVER_IDENTITY_TOKEN, and HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_BEARER_TOKEN as secrets.
  • Prefer file-based secrets: set HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_BEARER_TOKEN_SRC and mount it read-only.

Operational notes:

  • If the container is in a crash/restart loop after the broker step (for example due to invalid config or broken plugins), you may mint tokens repeatedly. To reduce token minting in crash/restart loops, set HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_MIN_RETRY_INTERVAL_SECONDS.
  • If you run a large fleet, consider protecting the broker with an HTTP bearer token and applying startup jitter on your orchestration side to avoid many servers contacting the broker at once.

Minimal example (Docker Compose):

services:
  hytale:
    environment:
      HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_ENABLED: "true"
      HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_URL: "http://broker:8080"
      HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS: "10"

With HTTP bearer token (recommended as file-based secret):

services:
  hytale:
    secrets:
      - broker_bearer
    environment:
      HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_ENABLED: "true"
      HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_URL: "http://broker:8080"
      HYTALE_SESSION_TOKEN_BROKER_BEARER_TOKEN_SRC: "/run/secrets/broker_bearer"

secrets:
  broker_bearer:
    file: ./secrets/broker_bearer_token

items.title: What the broker does not replace
items.text:
The game-server image still needs its JAR and assets before requesting broker tokens. Keep downloader credentials separate. The Compose snippets above assume that a broker is already running and reachable as broker; they do not deploy or authenticate one.

Follow the broker setup guide to deploy it and preserve its own data directory. Do not expose its API publicly without access controls. For native updates, use a direct server OAuth login or keep the startup downloader update model. See updates.

items.title: Hyrouter integration
items.text: Hyrouter accepts a Hytale connection and chooses a backend using routing rules and optional plugins. It sends a client referral, after which the player connects to the backend directly.

items.title: What to configure
items.text:
• Publish the router's UDP entrypoint for players.
  • Give every selected backend an address and UDP port reachable by those players. A Docker-internal service name is usually not reachable by a remote game client.
  • Authenticate each game server independently, using its own persisted login or the broker integration.
  • Configure routing and any referral-validation plugin using the router's documentation.

The router does not forward gameplay traffic. Allowing traffic only to the router while hiding all backend addresses behind an unreachable private network does not provide a working referral setup.

items.title: Diagnose a failed referral
items.text:
First verify a direct client connection to the selected backend. If direct access works, inspect the router's selected target, advertised address, TLS/QUIC negotiation and referral logs. Test with the client version supported by your router release.

A successful doctor report on the backend does not test the router's handshake or prove that a remote client can follow a referral.

For full configuration, deployment and plugin options, use the Hyrouter documentation. This site documents how the server image fits into the stack; the router repository remains the source for its own settings.
